title: What Is Directional Bias?

launchpad.outcome: Tell an observation, a working thesis and a prediction apart, and know what a real thesis answers.

slides.headline: Bias isn’t a feeling.
slides.line: It’s a thesis you can explain, and invalidate.

slides.heading: Which one is a useful trading bias?
slides.body: Same chart. Three ways to talk about it:

beats.title: Thesis
beats.line: “I’m more interested in bullish continuation, unless price changes the story.”

check.prompt: Which one is a useful trading bias?

options.label: The thesis
options.why: It’s based on structure, and it says what would change it.

options.label: The prediction
options.feedback: A prediction gets defended. A thesis updates.

options.label: The observation
options.feedback: Observations are the evidence. The thesis is what you build from them.

items.text: Price closed above the previous 4H swing.
items.why: Pure fact. Anyone can point to it.

items.text: Current structure supports bullish continuation unless supporting structure fails.
items.why: Conditional, based on structure, with a way to be wrong.

items.text: NQ is definitely hitting the external high today.
items.why: “Definitely” is doing a lot of work. The market doesn’t owe anyone that.

items.text: Price is trading in the lower half of the 4H room.
items.why: Location is something you can see.

items.text: I called bullish this morning, so I’m bullish all day.
items.why: That’s loyalty to an opinion, not a read of current structure.

items.text: I favor bearish continuation while price holds below the 1H lower high.
items.why: Direction, evidence, and a condition that would change it.

slides.heading: A real thesis answers seven questions.
slides.body: Each one gets a place on your Analysis Board.
slides.punch: You’ll fill every one of these in by the end of this section.

slides.quote: Your bias is allowed to change when price changes.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what’s the difference between a bias and a prediction?
slides.modelAnswer: A prediction says what price will do. A bias is a conditional thesis built on current structure, and it changes when the structure that supports it changes.

takeaways: Thesis = a conditional read built on structure.
Prediction = certainty the market never promised.
remember: Bias is a conditional directional thesis based on current structural evidence.
